DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 82 s. 2022 JUL 11 2022 Hon. REYNALDO S. TAMAYO, JR. Governor Province of South Cotabato Office of the Provincial Governor City of Koronadal Dear Governor Tamayo: This refers to your letter dated March 7, 2022 requesting for this Department's legal opinion concerning the action of the sanggunian in dismissing your administrative complaints for Grave of Abuse of Authority and Dishonesty against the incumbent Municipal Mayor of T'boli, Mayor Dibu S. Tuan. As culled from your Letter, hereunder are the pertinent factual antecedents: • The aforesaid administrative complaints were filed in August 6, 2021 in consonance with Sections 60 and 61 of the Local Government Code of 1991; • The SP, through the its Secretary furnish the respondent Mayor Tuan with copies of the complaints, along with its attachments through registered mail and was received by the respondent on September 3, 2021; On September 14, 2021 Mayor Tuan requested for extension of time to file answer for a period of fifteen (15) days or until October 3, 2021. However, on October 1, 2021 , Mayor Tuan through counsel again asked for another fifteen (15) days to file his answer; On October 18, 2021, Mayor Tuan through counsel filed a Motion to Dismiss on the ground that the complainant failed to furnish copies of the complaints to the respondent and the office of the DILG in compliance to SP Ordinance No. 1 series of 2001 and violating his right of due process; • You furnished the SP eighteen (18) sets of copies of the administrative complaints and its attachments not only once but twice- first on September 14, 2021 and on October 1, 2021; • The SP, however, dismissed your complaint against Mayor Tuan on the ground cited by Mayor Tuan (Item 4 hereof); Premised from the foregoing, arose your request for this Department's opinion on the following issues, to wit: I. Whether or not the action of the SP in dismissing Gov. Tamayo's Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

complaints against Mayor Tuan by reason of the former's alleged failure to fumish copies of the complaints to the respondent is valid? 2. Which shall prevail, Section 61 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 which provides clear guidelines in the filing of the administrative complaints or Section 5 of the SP Ordinance No. I series of 2001 which requires the complainants to fumish copies of the complaints to the respondent and the DILG? 3. Was the act of the SP in furnishing copies of the complaints to the respondent substantial compliance to the Local Govemment Code and SP Ordinance No. I series of 2001, thus the need to proceed with the conduct of the investigation is imperative? 4. Whether or not it is the responsibility and duty of the SP to fumish copies of the administrative complaints to the respondent and the office of the DILG being the office mandated by the Local Govemment Code to conduct investigation for administrative complaints against elective officials of the province? 5. Whether or not the SP is liable for violation of Article 126 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code for its unreasonable failure to commence the investigation within the prescribed period (120 days) after the receipt of the complaint by the respondent which was September 3, 2021 ? And 6. Whether or not the respondent should have been declared and deemed to have waived his right to file answer for his deliberate failure to file his answer and for his intentional delay by asking additional thirty (30) days extension of time to file answer in violation of Article 126 of the IRR of the Local Govemment Code of 1991? Foremost, it is to be remarked that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid any act committed by the sanggunian members which is alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred as the Code) or other applicable laws. Notwithstanding, we shall address the foregoing queries for purposes of academic discussions. It appears that the first third, and fourth queries are interrelated, hence we deemed it apt to address them in one comprehensive discussions. With that said, attention is respectfully directed to the pertinent provisions of the Code, thus: "Section 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Page 2 of 4

Office of the President; (b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the sangguniang panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and (c) A complaint against any elective barangay official shall be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory." The above-quoted provision of the Code provides for the procedure for the filing of administrative complaints against erring local elective officials, such as municipal mayors. Nowhere in the Code does it provide that the complainant shall furnish a copy of his verified complaints to the respondent. What is actually required by law to initiate administrative complaint against an erring local elective official is a verified complaint to be filed before the appropriate disciplining authority. It behooves now upon the concerned disciplining authority to furnish a copy, or more aptly, inform the person complained of regarding the case being filed against him in order to give him opportunity to answer such complaint and ultimately defend himself adequately. Section 62 (a) of the Code provides that: "Within seven (7) days after the administrative complaint is filed, the Office of the President or the sanggunian concerned, as the case may be, shall require the respondent to submit his verified answer within fifteen (15) days from receipt thereof, and commence the investigation of the case within ten (IO) days after receipt of such answer of the respondent." (Emphasis supplied) This Department submits that the duty of the sanggunian concerned in requiring the respondent to submit his verified answer within such period, as prescribed in the above-cited provision, is concomitant with the duty to inform the respondent of the complaints filed against him, which may include furnishing the respondent with the copy of such complaint. Accordingly, this Department opines that the action of SP in dismissing your complaints on the ground that you failed to furnish copies of the complaints to the respondent is misplaced. Going now to the 2nd issue, this Department submits that the Local Government Code of 1991 shall prevail. It is a fundamental principle that municipal ordinances are inferior in status and subordinate to the laws of the state (Batangas CATV, INC. v. Court of Appeals, G.R. No. 138810 dated September 29, 2004). Anent the fifth Article 126 (2) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Code is categorical when it provides that: "Unreasonable failure to commence the investigation within the prescribed period by the person or persons assigned to investigate shall be ground for disciplinary action." Here, we are of the view that failure of herein concerned SP to commence the Page 3 of 4

investigation of the administrative complaint filed before it within the prescribed period provided under the Code may be a ground for dereliction or neglect of duty pursuant to Section 60 of the Code. Coming now to the the same shall be answered in the affirmative. Article 126 (I) of the IRR of the Code states: "Unreasonable failure of the respondent to file his verified answer within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the complaint shall be considered a waiver of his rights to present evidence in his behalf." This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: •d 'Kiri I INGAN Underse r tary for Local Government OUSLG/MLVLLLS-LRALLD/jam Dir.
